section_summary: This section documents foreign oil companies’ responses to proposed petroleum controls in Japan and an oil sales monopoly in Manchuria in late 1934. Company correspondence weighs quotas, crude oil tenders, stockholding rules and possible refining arrangements, while American and British officials debate the timing and form of diplomatic representations. Several company enclosures and a conversation memorandum appear more than once.

people.name: Mr. Hashimoto
people.role: Oil company president and, according to one letter, head of the Manchukuo Oil Monopoly Bureau

people.name: Stanley K. Hornbeck
people.role: Chief, Division of Far Eastern Affairs

people.name: W. C. Teagle
people.role: Standard Oil Company of New Jersey representative

people.name: Mrs. Hull
people.role: Telephone intermediary for the Secretary of State

subfiles.title: Letter on proposed Manchukuo oil monopoly
subfiles.from: J. W. Loucks, Standard-Vacuum Oil Company, Mukden
subfiles.about: Reports monopoly officials’ proposed distribution system and urges coordinated company and diplomatic opposition.
subfiles.summary: The proposed monopoly would buy output from Fushun and Dairen, tender any shortfall to established companies, and take over much of their equipment. Loucks urges an early meeting with company and embassy representatives and publicity about the scheme.

subfiles.title: Oil Monopoly—Manchoukuo
subfiles.from: F. J. Twogood, Standard-Vacuum Oil Company, New York
subfiles.about: Seeks views on a possible control-law compromise and General Hishikari’s resignation.
subfiles.summary: Twogood favors percentage based quotas if compromise becomes necessary and asks whether Hishikari’s resignation changes the outlook.

subfiles.title: Consul Vincent’s letter on the Manchurian oil monopoly
subfiles.from: John Carter Vincent, American Consulate, Dairen
subfiles.about: Recommends a common foreign-company proposal before the monopoly law takes effect.
subfiles.summary: Vincent doubts that monopoly officials are bluffing. He suggests accepting reasonable controls and a reduced market share as a possible basis for negotiation, with company and embassy representatives first presenting their case in Japan.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Kersey F. Coe on petroleum problems
subfiles.about: Records Coe’s discussion of Japanese and Manchurian oil controls with Mr. Mackay.
subfiles.summary: Coe discusses provisional import plans, a proposed company conference in Shanghai, and possible joint refining in Japan. He reports that Standard-Vacuum, Shell and Texas do not intend to bid on a Manchurian crude oil tender. Mackay raises reports about petroleum distribution at Harbin.

subfiles.title: Coe letter on diplomatic action and stockholding
subfiles.from: Kersey F. Coe, Standard-Vacuum Oil Company
subfiles.about: Urges diplomatic representations before oil company delegates reach Japan and quotes Hashimoto on stockholding costs.
subfiles.summary: Coe gives the delegates’ expected travel dates and quotes Hashimoto’s public criticism of the law’s six month stockholding requirement.

subfiles.title: Reply to Coe on petroleum controls
subfiles.from: Stanley K. Hornbeck, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Coe’s letter and notes official attention to further representations.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck says American and British officials are considering further representations and notes Japanese company objections to the law.

subfiles.title: Return of Dundas correspondence
subfiles.about: Returns Dundas’s letter and enclosures after copying them for State Department files.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck thanks Teagle for lending Dundas’s letter and enclosures.

subfiles.title: Dundas letter to Teagle on Japan
subfiles.about: Forwards cables on Japanese oil controls and a crude oil tender for Manchukuo.
subfiles.summary: Dundas forwards London exchanges and a Yokohama cable, noting Coe’s State Department meeting.

subfiles.title: Yokohama cable on Manchuria Oil Company crude tender
subfiles.about: Reports a restricted invitation to bid on crude oil and recommends declining.
subfiles.summary: Nippon Oil seeks roughly 13,000 tons of crude for Manchuria Oil Company. After embassy consultations, the sender recommends no bid and asks for prompt guidance.

subfiles.title: Wilkinson telephone message on Form 4 and joint refining
subfiles.about: Proposes conditional Form 4 filing and coordinated diplomatic and company talks.
subfiles.summary: Wilkinson proposes a provisional import return that does not commit the companies to stockholding rules. He asks about future market shares and foreign owned refineries, and proposes that Godber, Walden and Parker confer in Shanghai before proceeding to Japan.

subfiles.title: Reply to ASDEBATIC, London
subfiles.about: Accepts a qualified Form 4 return and rejects bidding on Manchurian crude.
subfiles.summary: The sender supports prior diplomatic action, defers joint refining, and asks that no crude oil bid be made.

subfiles.title: Dundas letter to Teagle on Japan, second copy
subfiles.about: Again forwards the London exchanges and Yokohama crude tender cable.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the Dundas letter on page 331.

subfiles.title: Yokohama crude tender cable, second copy
subfiles.about: Again reports the crude oil tender and recommends declining.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the cable on pages 332–333.

subfiles.title: Wilkinson telephone message, second copy
subfiles.about: Again proposes conditional Form 4 filing and coordinated negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the telephone message on pages 334–336.

subfiles.title: Reply to ASDEBATIC, second copy
subfiles.about: Again accepts a qualified Form 4 return and declines the crude tender.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the cable on page 337.

subfiles.title: Dundas letter to Teagle on Japan, third copy
subfiles.about: Again forwards the London exchanges and Yokohama crude tender cable.
subfiles.summary: Third copy of the Dundas letter.

subfiles.title: Yokohama crude tender cable, third copy
subfiles.about: Again reports the crude oil tender and recommends declining.
subfiles.summary: Third copy of the Yokohama cable.

subfiles.title: Wilkinson telephone message, third copy
subfiles.about: Again proposes conditional Form 4 filing and coordinated negotiations.
subfiles.summary: Third copy of the Wilkinson message.

subfiles.title: Reply to ASDEBATIC, third copy
subfiles.about: Again accepts a qualified Form 4 return and declines the crude tender.
subfiles.summary: Third copy of the reply on page 337.

subfiles.title: Confidential transmission of conversation memoranda
subfiles.from: R. Walton Moore, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Sends five memoranda about oil situations in Japan and Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: Moore confidentially forwards memoranda of conversations with Wiggin and Coe.

subfiles.title: London telegram on British oil diplomacy
subfiles.about: Explains British plans for informal representations and conditions for company delegates to visit Japan.
subfiles.summary: British officials say Clive will consult Grew before further representations. British company delegates in Shanghai will proceed to Japan only if Tokyo’s response warrants it.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Sir Ronald Lindsay
subfiles.about: Records a discussion of a British inquiry prompted by press comments about Manchukuo oil.
subfiles.summary: Lindsay explains the inquiry’s origin; Hornbeck asks for clearer statements of its subject.

subfiles.title: Conversation with Sir Ronald Lindsay, second copy
subfiles.about: Repeats the discussion of the British inquiry.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate of the memorandum on pages 355–356.

subfiles.title: Letter to Secretary Hull on the oil situation
subfiles.about: Recommends waiting before warning American oil companies away from Japan and Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: Hornbeck reports company consultations and plans to send representatives to Japan. He favors a temporary pause, awaiting a British initiative and company negotiations, while cautioning against commitments involving large investments or long delivery periods.

subfiles.title: Proposed warning to American oil companies
subfiles.about: Suggests warning American oil interests against entering Japan and Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: Proposes a warning after unsuccessful representations to Japan.

subfiles.title: Comment on British leadership and boycott proposal
subfiles.about: Supports having Britain lead oil discussions and considers a milder alternative to a government boycott.
subfiles.summary: Hull favors British leadership and possible alternatives to a government boycott.

subfiles.title: Grew telegram summarizing British aide-mémoire
subfiles.about: Summarizes a planned British approach concerning the Petroleum Industry Law.
subfiles.summary: Clive seeks parallel American action before presenting a provisional British aide-mémoire. It argues that annual operating plans, refinery permissions, official intervention and stockholding requirements leave British companies uncertain about future business and investment.

subfiles.title: Instruction to Grew to await further guidance
subfiles.about: Directs Grew to defer action on Clive’s proposed approach.
subfiles.summary: The Department asks Grew to inform Clive that instructions will follow.

subfiles.title: Department telegram to Tokyo on British coordination
subfiles.about: Explains London discussions and argues for delaying another formal approach to Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Department clarifies that Dooman had no authority to agree to British proposals. It favors company coordination and an informal introduction of oil representatives before another government démarche, and asks Grew for contrary recommendations if he disagrees.

subfiles.title: Department telegram to London requesting clarification
subfiles.about: Questions the British plan for another approach before company delegates meet Japanese officials.
subfiles.summary: The Department asks London to explain a seeming change in British strategy and seek clear Foreign Office views. It favors informal introductions first and directs that Dooman cease appearing in the matter outside the embassy.

subfiles.title: File note on Grew’s November 12 despatch
subfiles.about: Cross-references Grew’s despatch on developments under Japan’s Petroleum Industry Law.
subfiles.summary: The abstract reports a dispute over import and storage plans, the six month stockholding rule, and Japan’s October 31 memorandum to foreign missions.

subfiles.title: File note on Grew’s November 27 telegram
subfiles.about: Cross-references Grew’s telegram urging stronger representations on oil controls.
subfiles.summary: The note points to Grew’s proposed formal recapitulation of American objections.

subfiles.title: Grew telegram urging renewed representations
subfiles.about: Argues for a formal American approach on Japanese and Manchurian petroleum measures.
subfiles.summary: Grew urges a firmly worded recapitulation to maintain a united front with Britain and defend American commercial interests and prestige. He notes the substantial American share of Manchurian oil sales but cautions that repeated protests without practical support may lose force.

subfiles.title: Bingham telegram clarifying British intentions
subfiles.about: Distinguishes British informal representations from assistance to company delegates.
subfiles.summary: British officials say Clive’s proposed brief is an informal representation, while special British company delegates will stay in Shanghai unless talks in Tokyo improve prospects. Bingham identifies a difference between British and American company expectations.

subfiles.title: Department telegram to London on next oil démarche
subfiles.about: Reasserts the Department’s preferred sequence for oil company talks and government representations.
subfiles.summary: The Department asks the embassy to clarify British views promptly. It favors an oral introduction of company representatives before further representations, but says it could support parallel informal talks suggested by Grew if Britain prefers that course. The telegram continues beyond page 394.
